supporting_observations.claim: WS-BCARTER-01 (10.30.10.22) made recurring connections to 10.30.20.30:8080 at 13:30:03, 13:36:22, 13:41:10, 13:46:34, 13:51:47, 13:55:57, 14:01:14 and 14:06:22 UTC. These records support approximately periodic proxy connections, but do not identify their external destinations.

Six recurring connections between 13:36 and 14:01 have similar volumes: 5,722–5,960 originator bytes and 30,202–30,287 responder bytes. This is consistent with repetitive automated activity, but does not distinguish legitimate polling from malicious beaconing.

Separate traffic at 14:10:02 is explicitly identified as a SharePoint API GET and correlated to chrome.exe through client source port 55716. This attribution applies to that connection, not to the earlier recurring connections.

The recurring-flow records establish timing and volume, but provide neither external destination nor initiating process. They therefore do not support choosing malicious beaconing or an approved updater as the explanation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The recurring connection records contain only the workstation-to-proxy leg, labeled service=http; they do not independently establish outbound HTTPS destinations, URLs, TLS details or proxy outcomes (T005-00098, T005-00126, T005-00148, T005-00166, T005-00184, T005-00196, T005-00205, T005-00212).

No matching process-attribution or proxy request records for those recurring connections are supplied. Attribution available for the later SharePoint connection cannot fill that gap (T005-00305 through T005-00309).
claims_not_established: Whether the recurring connections reached update.chartmate-imaging.com or originated from the inventory-listed ChartMate updater.
Whether the recurring connections represent command-and-control, exfiltration, legitimate update checks or another activity.
Whether the recurring connections share a single external destination or initiating process.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve proxy CONNECT/request records for the recurring timestamps, including destination, action, client source port and tunnel ID, and correlate them to the Zeek flows.
Retrieve endpoint network events identifying the initiating processes for source ports 53375, 62813, 56404, 56154, 49216, 49730, 50686 and 60971.

If an updater is identified, verify its executable signature, hash, process ancestry and application logs against the approved installation; otherwise investigate the identified process and destinations.
